title: Data centres sustain US copper demand amid tariff decision wait
author: Michael Finch, Benjamin Roche
text:
The race to build data centres is keeping US copper demand running hot, even as the market waits on Washington’s decision on refined copper tariffs, delegates heard at the American Copper Council (ACC) Fall Meeting in Miami (10–13 November).

Wire and cable producers and tube manufacturers at the meeting reported record orders, driven by the US data centre build-out. Copper makes up only 0.5–1% of data centre capex, so developers are not held back by elevated prices and are ordering freely to secure enough material.

“They just don’t care how much is left on reels after construction has finished, what they care about is delivering on time,” one US wire and cable producer told Benchmark.
